forces.title: Massive investment in crude oil tankers for energy security.
forces.description: India plans a substantial investment of Rs. 85,600 crore (US$ 10 billion) to acquire 112 crude oil tankers by 2040. This strategic move aims to enhance the nation's energy security and reduce its dependence on foreign-owned fleets, directly driving growth and opportunities within the LNG Transport (shipping vessels) component of the midstream sector.

forces.title: Natural gas assets seen as bankable lever for meeting electricity demand.
forces.description: Utilities executives worldwide are prioritizing 'adding natural gas' assets as one of the top five fastest and most bankable levers to meet surging electricity demand, particularly from data centers and AI. This indicates a continued need for gas transmission infrastructure to support power generation.

forces.title: Gas demand highly sensitive to macro, policy, and alternative costs.
forces.description: Natural gas demand faces significant uncertainty, with swings of 20% across scenarios due to macro conditions, national policies, and the cost competitiveness of renewables or nuclear. This volatility creates a risk of stranded or underutilized gas transmission and LNG infrastructure assets, particularly with stricter climate policies favoring clean firm options.

forces.title: Plateauing fossil fuel demand pressures marginal infrastructure assets.
forces.description: As global fossil fuel demand plateaus, infrastructure operators, including those in midstream, will face increasing pressure. Only low-cost, low-emissions assets are expected to remain profitable, while marginal assets will struggle. This trend necessitates strategic shifts towards capital discipline and optimizing asset portfolios for efficiency and lower emissions.

forces.title: Monetizing logistics assets and enhanced trading capabilities create value.
forces.description: Geopolitical uncertainty and high price volatility in oil, LNG, and refined products increase the potential for value creation from skilled trading functions and logistics assets. Rethinking monetization strategies for midstream assets (storage, pipelines, LNG transport) allows operators to react quickly, capture arbitrage opportunities, and leverage short-term flexibility, boosting profitability.

forces.title: Government plans massive investment to expand gas pipeline network.
forces.description: The Government of India plans to invest Rs. 70,000 crore (US$ 9.97 billion) to expand the national gas pipeline network. This significant investment is part of a strategic plan to increase the share of natural gas in the primary energy mix from 6% to 15% by 2030 and a USD 67 billion strategic investment for the Indian gas sector over the next 5-6 years, driving growth for gas transmission infrastructure.

forces.title: India's growing energy demand and green transition drives LNG and gas infrastructure.
forces.description: India's ambition to drive 35% of global energy demand growth over the next two decades, coupled with its green energy transition efforts, involves significant investment in natural gas, LNG, and hydrogen. This dual strategy aims to support decarbonization while meeting rising energy needs, leading to increased demand for LNG import capacity and gas transmission infrastructure.

forces.title: Strategic petroleum reserve expansion enhances storage terminal demand.
forces.description: The Union Budget FY26 allocated Rs. 5,597 crore (US$ 640.46 million) for Phase II of the Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Ltd (ISPRL) project. This investment aims to develop two new underground caverns for petroleum storage, directly stimulating demand and expansion opportunities for crude/product storage terminals in India.

forces.title: City gas expansion boosts demand for gas transmission infrastructure.
forces.description: City gas companies are aggressively expanding India’s gas sector by targeting new LNG stations and aiming to increase gas's share in the energy mix. This expansion, including a target of 126.3 million PNG connections and 18,336 CNG stations by 2034, will significantly boost demand for gas transmission networks to supply these burgeoning city gas distribution areas.

forces.title: Digital integration of terminal systems crucial for cash flow efficiency.
forces.description: Disconnected IT systems across the oil and gas supply chain, particularly impacting terminals and logistics, lead to significant inefficiencies like mismatched data and billing delays. Implementing Terminal Automation System (TAS) with ERP integration and real-time movement of uplift data is critical to accelerate cash flow and optimize operations in the midstream sector.

viewpoints.title: Natural gas demand outlook is uncertain and highly sensitive to macro conditions.
viewpoints.description: Bain's analysis indicates that natural gas demand is not a guaranteed winner, exhibiting swings of approximately 20% across different scenarios. Its trajectory is highly sensitive to macro conditions, national policy choices, and the cost competitiveness of alternative energy sources like storage-enabled renewables or nuclear. While gas demand is expected to grow in 'perpetuate present dynamics' and 'divergent pathways' scenarios due to its flexibility for grids, it tapers sooner in the 'low-carbon scale' scenario.

viewpoints.title: India's natural gas consumption to remain robust with strong infrastructure growth.
viewpoints.description: The International Energy Agency (IEA) projects a solid medium-term outlook for natural gas consumption in India. This positive outlook is driven by expanding infrastructure and supportive environmental policies. Industrial consumers are expected to contribute significantly, accounting for 40% of India's net demand growth, complemented by increasing demand from residential, transport, and energy sectors.

viewpoints.title: Infrastructure operators face asset profitability challenges as fossil fuel demand plateaus.
viewpoints.description: Bain's outlook across all scenarios suggests that as fossil fuel demand plateaus, the market will increasingly differentiate between profitable and struggling assets. Infrastructure operators, including midstream players, will need to possess low-cost and low-emission assets to remain profitable, as marginal assets are expected to struggle. This trend necessitates capital discipline and optimizing asset portfolios for efficiency and lower emissions.

viewpoints.title: India targets significant expansion in LNG import capacity to meet rising gas demand.
viewpoints.description: India, currently the fourth-largest LNG importer, plans to substantially increase its LNG import capacity to 50 million tonnes (MT) in the coming years. This expansion is driven by a domestic gas demand estimated to double by 2028, highlighting the country's growing reliance on imported liquefied natural gas to meet its energy needs.

viewpoints.title: Fragmented O&G supply chain systems create significant cash flow inefficiencies.
viewpoints.description: EY highlights that oil and gas supply chains, encompassing terminals and logistics (midstream components), operate with a patchwork of disconnected IT systems. This fragmentation leads to mismatched data, manual reconciliations, and delays, impacting order release, billing, and cash realization. Such inefficiencies can add 3-7 days to billing cycles, inflate disputes by 20-30%, and tie up millions across operations.
